title: Odile and the Orbit
premise: Tamsin Almeida, a xenolinguist exiled to the dying colony of Odile, has spent seven years recording a language that no longer exists in her dreams—and documenting a settlement the two great fleets have written off as lost. When gravity stutters for nine seconds across the entire system, she realizes someone is still watching Odile: both fleets believe the colony harbors a functioning jump-anchor, and each is racing to claim it. To prevent a war that would erase the last survivors, Tamsin and her estranged partner, engineer Sefa Okoye, must fabricate proof of an anchor that never existed, feeding a shared lie to two armadas while the jump window narrows. In the end, the lie collapses on schedule—but Tamsin broadcasts the colony's true inheritance, its recorded language and lives, into the window itself, forcing both fleets to arrive at an empty world holding nothing but testimony, and giving the survivors time to scatter toward a future no one promised them.
about_author: Marguerite Okonkwo is the pen name of a former field linguist who spent a decade documenting endangered languages before turning to science fiction. She writes from a coastal town where the fog rolls in like a slow transmission from somewhere far away.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. During a routine recording session in Odile's failing hydroponics bay, gravity flickers out for exactly nine seconds; water, seeds, and people hang suspended. The beat is quiet dread—Tamsin realizes the flicker was too precise to be natural, and that someone out there just tested the dark.

chapters.title: The Colony That Forgot Itself
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, with flashbacks. She walks Odile's half-abandoned habitats, cataloguing the 214 remaining colonists and the language only she still dreams in. Emotional beat: elegy. We learn why she was exiled here and what her recordings are really for—a message no one may ever receive.

chapters.title: Sefa's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Sefa Okoye's POV. The colony's chief engineer calculates they have four years of power, maybe five. She and Tamsin argue about whether to petition the fleets for rescue or keep broadcasting silence. Beat: love strained by duty—two people who once shared everything now defending opposite survival strategies.

chapters.title: What the Telescopes Saw
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Cross-referencing the nine-second event with old survey data, she finds the flicker originated from a relay neither fleet admits owning. A single encrypted ping answered it—from inside Odile's own dead comms array. Beat: the chill of realizing the invisible has been observed all along.

chapters.title: The Anchor That Isn't
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Deep beneath the original landing site, they find the wrecked frame of a jump-anchor the first colonists abandoned unfinished. Sefa understands instantly: to any fleet sensor, it could look almost real. Beat: terrible hope—the discovery that saves them might also doom them.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Alternating POV via intercepted fleet traffic (rendered through Tamsin's translation). Both the Concord and the Meridian Compact have logged the gravity flicker and concluded Odile holds a working anchor. Beat: rising tension—the war hasn't started yet, but both sides have already drawn their maps.

chapters.title: The First Broadcast
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. On Sefa's plan, she transmits a forged anchor handshake using the dead array, buying credibility at the cost of invisibility. The colony votes, narrowly, to lie. Beat: moral vertigo—Tamsin, whose life has been devoted to truthful transcription, becomes the author of a fiction.

chapters.title: Children of the Long Night
chapters.summary: POV of Idris, a fourteen-year-old born on Odile who has never seen another world. He helps Tamsin record the elders' stories, asking the questions adults are afraid to ask. Beat: tenderness and ache—the inheritance theme made flesh in a generation that will inherit whatever the lie buys them.

chapters.title: Concord Vanguard
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The Concord scout ship arrives in-system, polite and armed, requesting 'verification protocols.' Sefa plays host while secretly rerouting power to make the dead anchor read warm. Beat: white-knuckle hospitality—every conversation is a minefield walked in borrowed authority.

chapters.title: The Language Under the Floor
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A Concord xenolinguist, Vess Andrade, recognizes fragments of Tamsin's recordings and approaches her privately—not as an enemy but as the last other speaker of a dying tongue. Beat: unexpected intimacy; Tamsin finds a mirror and a threat in the same person.

chapters.title: Compact Shadow
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. The boy spots a Meridian stealth skiff parked in the asteroid belt, watching the Concord ship watch them. Neither fleet knows the other is here yet. Beat: dread compounding—the lie now has to hold against two audiences who might compare notes at any moment.

chapters.title: Handshake, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The Meridian Compact reveals itself with a hard ultimatum: surrender the anchor or be treated as Concord assets. Sefa stalls by claiming the anchor requires 'colonist attunement'—a fiction invented on the spot. Beat: improvisation at the edge of collapse; the lie grows teeth.

chapters.title: What Tamsin Dreamed
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Sleepless between negotiations, she dreams fully again in the dead language for the first time in years—and wakes understanding something crucial: the anchor's original builders left a warning encoded in its frame. Beat: revelation braided with grief; the past speaks at the worst possible moment.

chapters.title: The Warning in the Frame
chapters.summary: Sefa and Tamsin, dual POV. Decoded, the builders' warning says the anchor was abandoned because activating it here would tear the local jump corridor unstable—endangering every ship in-system. Beat: horror—the weapon both fleets want is a trap aimed at whoever pulls the trigger.

chapters.title: Vess's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Vess offers to falsify Concord's verification report in exchange for Tamsin's full linguistic archive—an act of treason against her own fleet. Beat: love against duty refracted through a stranger; Tamsin must decide whether trust is a luxury survivors can't afford.

chapters.title: The Jump Window Opens
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The corridor stabilizes; both fleets begin final approach, each believing the other will strike first. The colony has seventy-two hours before the window closes and the pretense becomes unsustainable. Beat: countdown pressure—every chapter from here runs on borrowed seconds.

chapters.title: Evacuation Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. The colonists quietly prepare lifeboats for a scattering with no destination, hiding the preparations from both fleets' sensors. Idris records his own voice into Tamsin's archive. Beat: quiet courage—the price of survival paid in advance by people who may never collect.

chapters.title: The Lie Breaks
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Concord and Compact ships detect each other simultaneously; verification reports contradict; weapons arm. Vess's forgery is exposed, and both fleets demand the truth from Odile within the hour. Beat: climax igniting—the moment the fiction dies and only truth or fire remains.

chapters.title: Broadcast Everything
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, climax. With the window closing, Tamsin transmits the entire archive—seven years of a dead language, 214 lives, the builders' warning, the whole unvarnished record—on every channel, addressed to no one and everyone. Beat: transcendence through testimony; the one thing she cannot lie about is what she loved.

chapters.title: Ships in the Corridor
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Both fleets hesitate at the threshold of an unstable corridor, confronted with evidence that the prize is a tomb. Shots are not fired; blame is deferred; the window closes with both armadas intact and empty-handed. Beat: exhausted relief—the war that didn't happen, and why.

chapters.title: Scattering
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. The colonists launch in small ships toward uncertain refuges, carrying copies of the archive. Vess defects to stay behind with Tamsin's recordings; some colonists choose to remain on Odile regardless. Beat: bittersweet dispersal—survival as a verb, not a place.

chapters.title: Dreaming in Translation
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, resolution. On the last ship out, Tamsin listens to the archive playing back and finally dreams in human words again—the dead language now living in thousands of fleet databases, translated, argued over, remembered. Beat: peace earned at cost; inheritance fulfilled; love outlasting duty.
